lessons.lesson: Review every held position on every run, including days with no trade: distance from price to the invalidation, earnings dates now inside the 5-day window versus what the thesis says, and thesis text that has gone stale. Where an invalidation clause is qualitative (e.g. 'exchange failure'), state in the reasoning whether it has tripped, and why. Write the re-anchored level or date into the decision reasoning rather than only flagging it. When a held name gaps far from the price its stop was written against, re-anchor the stop to the close and to the gain, and name any stop within about 2% of the market together with the dated catalysts. Compute every stop distance and position weight from the latest mark in the inputs, say which mark was used, and after a large up day restate the dollar risk of a held-through-earnings position at its current weight. When a stop is re-anchored after a big run-up, or a stop or the SPY 200-day line is within about 10% of the mark, also state the distance on a mark 4-5% lower, since the inputs are pre-open and the day can move that far. For bond funds (BND, IEF), give the distance in daily-volatility units or as the yield move that would trip it instead, since 4-5% is weeks of normal moves for them. On a day with a dated macro print (CPI, payrolls, a Fed decision), say for every rate- or macro-conditioned clause whether it has tripped. What goes into stored thesis text is covered by L6.
